evidence.field: 形義通解; bronze forms and proposed lexical analyses
evidence.text: The entry describes bronze 真 as 貝 with 𠂈 as a phonetic element; it also reports forms using 鼎, which it says could be confused graphically with 貝, and a 真盤 form with added 丌. It reports He Linyi’s proposal that 真 was an early graph for 珍 ‘precious’, and Xie Mingwen’s account that 真 was borrowed for ‘true’, after which 珍 was formed with 玉 and 㐱. These are competing proposals, not a resolved origin. The entry associates 𠂈 with the ancient form of 殄 and with 顛, but does not independently establish the name of an object depicted by 𠂈.
evidence.kind: character-specific lexicographic/paleographic reference; source assertions and reported proposals
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 真

evidence.field: 字形探源; form sequence and proposed lexical origin
evidence.text: The study says 真 is not seen in oracle-bone inscriptions and first appears in Western Zhou bronzes. It describes early forms with 貝 and a sound element, forms with a lower element, and forms identified with 鼎. It traces the 貝 shape becoming 目-like in Spring and Autumn forms, with further Warring States changes. It presents Tang Lan’s proposal relating 真 to 殄. The study’s descriptions do not settle the word represented by the earliest bronze forms.
evidence.kind: paleographic study; source assertions and attributed proposal
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源（entry 134 真）

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry cites a Western Zhou bronze personal-name use on 真盤, which by itself does not establish the name’s spoken form or meaning. It cites Shuihudi Qin legal-question slip 49 for ‘actual/true’; Zhuangzi《秋水》 and 呂氏春秋《上農》 for ‘original/inherent nature’; and 荀子《非十二字》 for adverbial ‘indeed’. These citations establish separate reported uses, not their chronology or semantic derivation. Exact composition dates and manuscript-witness dating are not supplied in this entry.
evidence.kind: character-specific lexicographic reference citing inscription and texts
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 真

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Taiwan Ministry of Education
evidence.field: 眞 (真); seal-script interpretation and graphic status
evidence.text: The entry repeats Shuowen’s interpretation of seal-script 眞 through 匕, 目, 乚 and 八, and notes that the standard form 真 is treated as the proper form while 眞 is an alternate form. This is a later dictionary tradition and does not establish the original referent or word of the bronze graph.
evidence.title: A02768-003 眞 (真) — 教育部《異體字字典》

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK entry and search results for Baxter–Sagart and Unicode. The local 真 Baxter–Sagart row is *ti[n] / tsyin; no local 𠂈 row was supplied. Character-specific Unihan endpoints failed. The official general Unihan distribution page was inspected separately.

Search located the official Unicode versioned Unihan distribution. The directory page was inspected and lists Unihan.zip; direct data and character-specific records remained inaccessible, so local reading rows remain unverified externally.

gaps: Exact Unihan character records for 真 (U+771F), 𠂈 (U+2E88), and 眞 (U+771E) could not be opened; official directory confirms a versioned Unihan distribution but not their individual values.

The local Baxter–Sagart data has 真 (*ti[n], MC tsyin) but no 𠂈 row; a component-to-host comparison in the same reconstruction system cannot be made from the supplied local rows. Modern readings 𠂈 jié and 真 zhēn are not evidence of an ancient sound relationship.

The proposed depicted object and original name/pronunciation for 𠂈 remain unrecovered. This limits any claim that an independently named weapon or tool supplied a borrowed sound; it does not by itself rule out 𠂈 functioning as a sound element in the bronze compound.

Western Zhou bronze personal-name use is reported, but exact artifact chronology was not independently verified against excavation or catalogue records; the name does not reveal the spoken word or its meaning.

The cited Qin slip 49 and classical text citations show separate senses, but the sources inspected do not establish a full chronology, composition dates versus witness dates, or the semantic path among ‘true/actual’, ‘inherent nature’, and adverbial ‘indeed’.

The CUHK account and paleographic study differ in how they describe lower graphic features and stages. Their descriptions should remain source-attributed; no inscription image was independently inspected in this research pass.
